content_of_post_to_comment: American Alcohol Culture - I have questions, I want answers 1 My old man went to a wedding over the weekend - no open bar, and even soft drinks weren’t free, which is a first (he shelled out $4 for a tonic water and was not happy about it). I’ve been to many weddings in various countries and the only times I’ve encountered cash bars were in the US - in Europe and other parts of the world, it’s always open bar, in my experience. Thoughts? 2 We’ve now been invited over twice to people’s houses for barbecues. Both times, we were offered only non-alcoholic drinks. The first time, when they asked if I wanted anything to drink, I asked, “what beer do you have?” and they looked at me like I was nuts. Is this a faux pas? I’m not saying there’s anything wrong with this, but…I do find it unusual. Or perhaps I’m used to Europe and its debaucherous ways, where even at kids’ birthday parties the booze is flowing freely.
